source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies latent-confounded time-series graphs and proves a constant-size segment sufficient for identification decisions, with a bound depending on width and maximal lag.

The official abstract claims total-effect identification results for extended and ordinary SCGs and adjustment sets; it is an abstraction-of-time-series result rather than hidden-variable fixing completeness.
The paper gives complete causal-effect identification and a hedge characterization of nonidentifiable effects for a fixed causal graph.
The paper takes a PAG representing a Markov-equivalence class and proves a sound-and-complete algorithm and calculus for conditional-effect identification.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes linearity and no hidden confounding and gives a complete SCG result for direct effects with finite adjustment sets.
The paper distinguishes macro from micro queries and states soundness and completeness of do-calculus for macro total effects under latent confounding.

The paper gives necessary-and-sufficient common-adjustment conditions and a pseudo-linear decision algorithm under causal sufficiency, explicitly distinguishing global identification beyond adjustment as future work.
The paper derives influence-function and weight-based estimation strategies for identifiable effects in hidden-variable DAG models under independent-sample semiparametric theory.
The cited paper is the original modified-Bartlett positive-semidefinite HAC construction and its consistency result under a slowly growing bandwidth regime.
